description:
FILED s470br round 3 (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the FIRST full companion run of the
s470br batch.  A #1115 REGRESSION, bisected and probed.  NOT FIXED HERE -- the
round-3 work order forbade touching cl/.

THE NUMBER: `t/op/read.t` goes from **OK 2116/0** to **DIFF 1852/264**.
264 rows, and every one of them is a ` u` row of the file's read-into-buffer
matrix (the ones that do `binmode FH, "utf8"`).

BISECTED, each measured with `tools/run-perl-suite.pl op/read.t` in its own
`git worktree` (`env -C`, which is the form that survives an agent thread's
cwd reset):

    027ba9c  (main, before the batch)                      2116/0   OK
    3a89a5c  (#1115 + its review fixes, ONLY)              1852/264 DIFF
    24030f4  (after #1115 + #1116 + #1120)                 1852/264 DIFF
    f01dcd6  (the whole batch, at the merge point)         1852/264 DIFF

So it is #1115 (`9492ecb` + `3a89a5c`) alone.

THE CAUSE, probed against perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s470br/p-read.pl):

    my $value = join "", map { chr $_ } 253 .. 257;   # 3 latin-1 + 2 wide
    for my $lay ("utf8", ":utf8") {
      open FH, ">$f"; binmode FH, $lay; print FH $value; close FH;
      open FH, $f;    binmode FH, $lay; read(FH, my $buf, 10, 0);
      ...
    }

    perl 5.40.3   layer=utf8   filesize=10 read=5  buflen=5  ords=253,254,255,256,257
                  layer=:utf8  filesize=10 read=5  buflen=5  ords=253,254,255,256,257
    PCL HEAD      layer=utf8   filesize=10 read=10 buflen=10 ords=195,189,195,190,195,191,196,128,196,129
                  ...and "Wide character in print" on the WRITE side
                  layer=:utf8  filesize=10 read=5  buflen=5  ords=253,254,255,256,257
    PCL 027ba9c   both spellings 5/5 -- correct, BY ACCIDENT

**`binmode FH, "utf8"` -- a layer name with NO leading colon -- is not
recognised.**  perl accepts it (perlfunc binmode: the leading `:` is optional);
`%p-split-layers` splits on `:` and a colon-less string yields no layer, so the
handle stays a BYTE handle.  The write side then hands a wide character to a
byte stream (the %p-wide-char-upgrade repair fires and says so) and the read
side hands back the 10 UTF-8 octets where perl hands back the 5 characters.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: before #1115, `binmode` was a no-op AND the default
external format was UTF-8, so every ` u` row passed for the wrong reason.
#1115 made binmode real and the default bytes; the accident stopped.
`t/op/read.t` is in `t/op/`, and s470br round 1 ran only the `io/` and `uni/`
companion legs -- so nothing in the batch's own bars could see it.  This is
exactly the class the DECIDED s470 rule "the merge-time sweep is
NON-NEGOTIABLE for cl/ work" exists for.

THE FIX (sketch, NOT applied): `%p-split-layers` (or its caller in
`%p-binmode-impl`) must accept a layer list whose FIRST layer omits the leading
colon.  perl's rule, worth probing before writing it: the colon is optional
only for the whole-string single-layer spelling that `binmode` takes;
`open`'s 3-arg MODE always carries it.  Probe at least: `binmode FH, "utf8"`,
`binmode FH, ":utf8"`, `binmode FH, "raw"`, `binmode FH, "encoding(UTF-8)"`,
`binmode FH, "raw:utf8"`, and the two-arg `binmode FH` (no layer = :raw).

ACCEPTANCE: `tools/run-perl-suite.pl op/read.t` back to 2116/0 OK; the probe
above identical to perl in both spellings; a guard row in
`Pl/t/io-layers-01.t` (which already owns #1115's shapes) asserting the
colon-less spelling, failing on a pre-fix tree.


=== DONE (s470bv) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-06 in the s470bv worktree, commit 8fb91c3 (rebased onto main
9ee95f2).  ONE runtime commit, `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` + `Pl/t/io-layers-01.t` +
`docs/ir-spec.md` §7.7.

THE FIX, at the ONE place a layer string is split (rule 11).  perl's
PerlIO_parse_layers grammar, probed spelling by spelling against perl 5.40.3:
a layer NAME's leading colon is OPTIONAL, `:` and whitespace are both
SEPARATORS, an empty name is skipped, and an UNKNOWN name makes the whole call
FAIL (undef, $! = ENOENT) with NOTHING applied.  `%p-split-layers` was
rewritten to that grammar; `%p-split-open-mode` now splits on the SIGIL run and
returns the first unknown layer as a 4th value; `%p-binmode-impl` and
`%p-open-impl` fail as perl does; `p-use-open`'s word classifier no longer
requires the colon.  New helpers: `%p-layer-separator-p`, `%p-open-mode-char-p`,
`%p-layer-ef-or-announce`, `%p-io-errno-fail`.

MEASURED:
* t/op/read.t **1852/264 DIFF -> 2116/0 OK** (the task's acceptance).
* Guard `Pl/t/io-layers-01.t` 27 -> 36 rows; INVERSE on a `git archive 424cabc`
  extraction: 7 of the 9 new rows FAIL there (the other two assert grammar the
  old splitter happened to get right).
* Gate 213 files / 7342 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs rows failing.
* FULL perl-tests sweep `--jobs 4`: TOTAL 18646 = baseline (+0), GATE clean,
  0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, drops 5 = census.
* `tools/ir-host-leak.pl` 31 leaks here and 31 on a 9ee95f2 extraction of main.
* Companion 63-file `--jobs 1`: the ONLY file this change moves is op/read.t.

RESIDUE, filed, NOT fixed here:
* **#1270** -- the COMPILE-TIME half of the same grammar
  (`Pl::Parser::_use_open_layers`) still requires the leading colon, so
  `use open IO => "utf8"` is silently discarded.  A `Pl/` change, with its own
  bars.
* **#1271** -- a FAILED `open(my $fh, ...)` leaves the lexical undef where perl
  autovivifies the glob.
* `utf8::is_utf8` answering 1 on a byte-read string is ALREADY BLESSED in
  docs/not-supported.md ("The per-scalar UTF-8 flag"), so no task was filed.
subject: binmode FH, "utf8" -- a layer name with NO leading colon -- is not recognised, so the handle stays a BYTE handle (#1115 regression: t/op/read.t 2116/0 -> 1852/264)
